home.title: Sepsis and septic shock explained: an animated guide
home.description: An animated, cited guide to sepsis and septic shock: what it is, warning signs, Sepsis-3 and qSOFA, the first hour of treatment, and recovery after sepsis.

what.title: What is sepsis? Septic shock and how common it is
what.description: What sepsis and septic shock are under Sepsis-3, animated, with the global burden: 48.9 million cases and 11 million deaths a year, germs and sources.

immune.title: Sepsis immunology: PAMPs, TLR4, cytokines and NETs
immune.description: Animated sepsis immune cascade: PAMPs and DAMPs, TLR4 and NF-κB, cytokines, neutrophil NETs, immunoparalysis, and why anti-inflammatory trials failed.

endothelium.title: Sepsis, endothelium and DIC: leak, microclots, organs
endothelium.description: How sepsis sheds the glycocalyx, makes vessels leak, forms microclots and fails organs, with a teaching SIC and ISTH overt DIC score calculator.

shock.title: Shock and haemodynamics: cardiac output, MAP and shock types
shock.description: How blood pressure, cardiac output and vessel tone fit together, the four types of shock, MAP and the shock index, with animations and teaching calculators.

risk.title: Who is at risk of sepsis? Age, illness, immunity, pregnancy
risk.description: Who is more likely to get sepsis: babies and older adults, long-term illness, cancer, weak immunity, pregnancy, recent healthcare and unequal risk.

recognise.title: Recognising sepsis: warning signs and NEWS2 explained
recognise.description: The warning signs of sepsis in plain words, how a NEWS2 early warning score rises as someone deteriorates, and a teaching-only NEWS2 calculator.

definitions.title: qSOFA and SOFA scores: Sepsis-3 definitions explained
definitions.description: How sepsis was defined from SIRS in 1991 to Sepsis-3 in 2016 and SOFA-2, why qSOFA screens poorly, with teaching qSOFA and SOFA calculators.

tests.title: Lactate, blood cultures and procalcitonin in sepsis
tests.description: Why lactate rises in sepsis, what its thresholds mean, how blood cultures are taken and read, procalcitonin stop rules and rapid tests, as published.

firsthour.title: Sepsis Hour-1 bundle and time to antibiotics explained
firsthour.description: The Hour-1 sepsis bundle on an animated clock, what studies found on time to antibiotics, the EGDT trials from Rivers to PRISM, and the SEP-1 debate.

fluids.title: Fluids in sepsis: 30 mL/kg, Frank–Starling and the trials
fluids.description: Fluid resuscitation in septic shock: fluid responsiveness, leaky vessels, balanced crystalloids versus saline, albumin, starches and the restrictive trials.

pressors.title: Vasopressors and steroids in septic shock: MAP targets
pressors.description: Noradrenaline, vasopressin, adrenaline and angiotensin II explained, with MAP targets from SEPSISPAM and the 65 trial, and the hydrocortisone trials compared.

source.title: Sepsis source control and antibiotic stewardship explained
source.description: Draining the source of sepsis, the first antibiotic, de-escalation, 7-day courses, procalcitonin, prolonged infusions and antimicrobial resistance.

icu.title: Sepsis in intensive care: ventilation, dialysis, ICU trials
icu.description: Organ support in sepsis: lung-protective ventilation, prone positioning, oxygen, dialysis timing, glucose, transfusion, sedation, delirium and families.

othershock.title: Cardiogenic, hypovolaemic, obstructive & anaphylactic shock
othershock.description: Non-septic shock explained: heart attack shock and its trials, bleeding and tranexamic acid, tamponade and pulmonary embolism, and anaphylaxis adrenaline.

children.title: Sepsis in babies and children: signs, Phoenix criteria
children.description: Early signs parents notice, newborn early and late onset sepsis, the 2024 Phoenix criteria with a teaching calculator, and what FEAST showed about fluids.

maternal.title: Maternal sepsis: pregnancy, after birth and warning signs
maternal.description: Why pregnancy can hide sepsis, how common maternal sepsis is, group A strep after birth, obstetric warning scores and trials preventing infection.

after.title: Life after sepsis: post-sepsis syndrome, PICS and families
after.description: The year after sepsis: weakness, memory, mood, readmission, return to work and late risks, what helps recovery, and support for families and the bereaved.

nursing.title: Sepsis nursing care: NEWS2, escalation and bundles
nursing.description: Sepsis nursing: NEWS2 and escalation, cultures and antibiotics on time, urine output, vasopressor line care, CLABSI and CAUTI bundles, exam questions.

prevention.title: Preventing sepsis: hand hygiene, vaccines and early signs
prevention.description: How clean hands, line and catheter bundles, vaccines, care around birth and knowing the early signs prevent the infections that lead to sepsis.

frontier.title: Sepsis research: failed trials, endotypes and immunotherapy
frontier.description: From failed anti-inflammatory trials and vitamin C to sepsis endotypes, precision immunotherapy, rapid diagnostics and AI alerts, with evidence labels.

history.title: History of sepsis: Semmelweis, penicillin to Sepsis-3
history.description: An animated timeline of sepsis, from Semmelweis's handwashing, Lister and penicillin to SIRS, the Surviving Sepsis Campaign, Sepsis-3, Phoenix and SOFA-2.

review.title: Sepsis flashcards and mnemonics: qSOFA, Hour-1 bundle
review.description: Flip cards on sepsis and septic shock by part, with memory aids for qSOFA, Sepsis-3 and the Hour-1 bundle, each answer linked to its published source.

quiz.title: Sepsis quiz: definitions, shock, treatment and trials
quiz.description: Multiple-choice questions on sepsis and septic shock, from SIRS and qSOFA to fluids, vasopressors, steroids and recovery, each with a cited explanation.

glossary.title: Sepsis glossary: qSOFA, lactate, SIRS, PICS and more
glossary.description: A searchable glossary of about 100 sepsis and shock terms, from PAMPs and the glycocalyx to qSOFA, SOFA-2, procalcitonin, noradrenaline and PICS.

sources.title: Sepsis Companion sources: trials, guidelines, reviews
sources.description: Every reference behind the Sepsis Companion: trials, meta-analyses, Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines and drug labels, filterable by research area.
